text:
Predicates:
LunchAtCompany(x) ::: x has lunch in the company.
LunchAtHome(x) ::: x has lunch at home.
ScheduleMeeting(x) ::: x schedules a meeting with their customers.
AppearToday(x) ::: x appears in the company today.
WorkRemotely(x) ::: x works remotely from home.
Manager(x) ::: x is a manager.
InOtherCountry(x) ::: x is in another country.
Premises:
∀x (ScheduleMeeting(x) → AppearToday(x)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (LunchAtCompany(x) → ScheduleMeeting(x)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (LunchAtCompany(x) ⊕ LunchAtHome(x)) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or have lunch at home.
∀x (LunchAtHome(x) → WorkRemotely(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (InOtherCountry(x) → WorkRemotely(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
∀x (Manager(x) → ¬WorkRemotely(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(james) ∧ AppearToday(james)) ⊕ ¬(Manager(james) ∨ AppearToday(james)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
Conclusion:
LunchAtCompany(james) ::: James has lunch in the company.
